newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris, RJR settlement talks - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris, RJR settlement talks - WSJ.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp are in secret talks with plaintiffs over a settlement which would cover nearly all the industry's liability for smoking in return for advertising limits and a payment possibly totaling $300 billion over the next 25 years, the Wall Street Journal said.

According to people familiar with the negotiations, the companies are negotiating details which include accepting regulation by the FDA, banning cigarette billboards and ending the use pictures of people like the Marlboro Man, in ads, the paper said in Wednesday's electronic edition.
The newspaper said under the plan, smokers could seek payments from a large industry fund but would generally be forbidden to sue the cigarette companies.
Terms of the talks, which began about two weeks ago, could still change, the Journal said.

Philip Morris Chairman Geoffrey Bible and RJR Chairman Steven Goldstone attended the first day of talks, the paper said. The companies were negotiating on behalf of other major U.S. tobacco firm, B.A.T Industries unit Brown & Wiliamson and Loews Corp's Lorillard unit, the paper said, citing people familiar with the talks.
Deputy White House Counsel Bruce Lindsey has also been monitoring the talks, the paper said.
Both companies, which were not immediately available, declined to comment in the Journal report.
